label: US sanctions Russian oil, tankers
description: Biden Treasury sanctions Gazprom Neft, Surgutneftegas and 183 vessels; spread rose from 2.5 (10 Jan) to 4.5 (17 Jan).
mechanism: Seaborne Russian barrels stranded on sanctioned tankers; Asian/European buyers bid for Atlantic Basin replacement grades and freight jumps, lifting Dated Brent more than landlocked WTI.

label: Tariffs + OPEC+ surprise hike
description: Liberation Day tariffs (2 Apr) and OPEC+ tripling its May hike to 411 kb/d (3 Apr) crash oil; spread peaks 6.2 (1 Apr) and 5.9 (4 Apr). Widening began 1 Apr, before the tariffs.
mechanism: US-centric demand and recession fear plus China retaliation hit WTI slightly harder than Brent. Weak link: the move is small and partly predates the event.

label: OPEC+ accelerates hikes again
description: OPEC+ agrees a second accelerated 411 kb/d hike for June; the spread fell from 3.8 (30 Apr) to about 1 to 1.4 (7-16 May) as hike talk spread from late April.
mechanism: Extra OPEC+ medium-sour seaborne supply competes directly with Brent-linked grades in Europe/Asia, weakening Dated Brent vs inland WTI.

label: US strikes Iran nuclear sites
description: US B-2 strikes on Fordow/Natanz/Isfahan (21-22 Jun) during the 12-day Israel-Iran war; spread 5.0 on 23 Jun, then back to 2.4 after the 24 Jun ceasefire.
mechanism: Gulf supply/Hormuz risk premium sits in waterborne Brent; WTI fell faster on the Monday ceasefire headline. Short-lived, so not a large move.

label: Rosneft/Lukoil sanctions take effect
description: OFAC sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil (announced 22 Oct 2025) hit their 21 Nov wind-down deadline; spread jumped from 3.9 (21 Nov) to 5.7 (24 Nov) and 5.5 (28 Nov).
mechanism: Buyers of Russian crude (India, Turkey, China) scramble for non-Russian seaborne cargoes, bidding up Dated Brent-linked grades vs WTI. Timing fits the deadline, but no direct spread commentary was found.

label: Venezuela crude flows to US
description: After the US seizure of Venezuelan oil flows (3 Jan), the WTI discount to Brent widened for 7 straight sessions to the largest in 8 months; Tengiz/CPC disruptions (Dated Brent differential at a 15-month high on 13 Jan) added to it.
mechanism: More Venezuelan heavy crude heading to the US Gulf loosens US balances and pressures WTI; lost CPC Blend tightens the Med/North Sea and lifts Dated Brent.

label: South Pars hit; SPR release
description: Israel strikes South Pars (18 Mar) and Iran retaliates on Ras Laffan/Ras Tanura (19 Mar), and Iraq declares force majeure. IEA 400 mb release (US 172 mb SPR, announced 11-16 Mar) and Cushing at an 18-month high weigh on WTI. The futures spread hit an 11-year wide (12.05); Dated spot spread 7.7 to 22.0 (16-18 Mar).
mechanism: Gulf infrastructure losses tighten seaborne crude (Dated Brent up 3.8% vs WTI +0.1%). SPR barrels and Cushing builds land in the US, depressing WTI. The export arb opens but freight caps it.

label: Trump war speech: WTI spikes
description: After Trump's Iran war speech, WTI jumped 11% to $111.54 and closed above Brent futures (2 Apr). The spot spread fell from 23.8 (31 Mar) to 14.4 (2 Apr).
mechanism: Mostly curve timing: expiring May WTI vs June Brent in steep backwardation, plus a prompt US squeeze. The WTI leg rose, not Brent falling.

label: Dated Brent record $144
description: Platts Dated Brent hit a record $144.42 on 7 Apr. After the 8 Apr ceasefire, futures fell 13-16%, but Forties hit a record +$20.25 to Dated, and Dated sat about $27 over June futures. Spot spread 23.6 to 25.9 (7-8 Apr), 20.7 (10 Apr).
mechanism: Physical North Sea cargoes are the marginal replacement for stranded Gulf barrels, so prompt Dated Brent stayed squeezed while WTI (and futures) priced the ceasefire.

label: Iran declares Hormuz open
description: Iran's FM declares Hormuz open for the rest of the ceasefire; Brent -9 to -13%. Dated Brent spot fell $18 (116.6 to 98.6) and the spread fell 20.2 to 12.7.
mechanism: Reopening hits the prompt physical seaborne premium hardest, compressing Dated Brent vs WTI. Note: 20-21 Apr was flat (about 12.4); the drop was 17 Apr, and the spread rebounded to 18.7 on 22 Apr as talks faltered.

label: US-Iran deal hopes; CFDs crash
description: Reports of a near US-Iran deal (6 May) send oil down about 8-10%. Physical cargo premiums then collapsed: the Brent CFD 6-week spread fell from about $28 to $2.15 by mid-May. Spot spread fell from 12.9 (1 May) to 3.4 (7 May).
mechanism: Panic buying of prompt Atlantic cargoes ends, so the Dated Brent premium over futures (and over WTI) evaporates.

label: Reopening hopes; Cushing draws
description: Rubio says talks get 'every chance' (27 May) and hopes rise for Hormuz reopening within a month; Brent has its biggest monthly loss in 6 years. Meanwhile record US exports of 5.6 mb/d drain Cushing. Spread 1.7 on 29 May.
mechanism: The Brent risk premium unwinds, while WTI is held up by export pull and shrinking Cushing stocks.

label: Cushing <20mb + Islamabad MoU
description: Cushing stocks fell below 20 mb in mid-June (near tank bottoms, lowest since 2008), and the spot Brent-Cushing spread went negative. At the same time the US-Iran MoU (16-18 Jun) reopened Hormuz and Brent fell to its lowest since March. Spread -1.0 (18 Jun), -2.45 (22 Jun), -1.2 (2 Jul).
mechanism: WTI is priced at a landlocked hub: a near-empty Cushing plus record exports squeezes WTI, while Hormuz reopening floods the seaborne market and deflates Dated Brent. Together they invert the spread.

label: Houthis blockade Saudi shipping
description: Houthis declare a naval blockade of Saudi shipments (20 Jul) and strike two Saudi tankers off Al Shuqaiq (22-23 Jul); Brent tops $100. Spread 2.6 to 7.8 (21 Jul) and 12.2 (23 Jul).
mechanism: The Red Sea/Yanbu route is the main Hormuz bypass. Threatening it tightens seaborne crude to Europe/Asia and lifts Dated Brent; WTI is insulated.

label: East-West pipeline hit; Yanbu shut
description: After a record surge in Gulf ship attacks (10 Sep), drone strikes shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline (11 Sep) and halted Yanbu loadings into late Sep. Dated Brent spot peaked at $130.80 on 15 Sep. Spread 12.3 (9 Sep) to 17.4 (10 Sep) to 24.2 (16 Sep).
mechanism: Removing the Red Sea bypass takes ~5 mb/d of seaborne Saudi export capacity offline, an acute physical-cargo shock priced into Dated Brent, not WTI.

label: Saudi reroutes via Hormuz
description: Reports that Saudi Arabia routed more crude through Hormuz after the pipeline loss; oil fell 17% over five days. Spot spread 24.2 to 18.0 (17 Sep).
mechanism: Replacement seaborne supply eases the Dated Brent squeeze.

label: 7-day plan; WTI spot outlier
description: Spread hit 30.8 on 25 Sep because EIA WTI spot printed 85.23 (-10.7 in a day), then 99.37 on 28 Sep. Brent spot barely moved. Araghchi's 7-day plan (25 Sep) is the only same-day event; no reported WTI crash matches.
mechanism: Likely a one-day WTI spot data quirk rather than a real move. Treat as unexplained.

label: Gulf flows top pre-war
description: Kpler shows Gulf flows of 19.5-22.5 mb/d on 27-29 Sep (Saudi loadings plus the US-escorted ADNOC shuttle), with 'exports hit pre-war levels' headlines on 30 Sep. Spread fell from 18.7 to 15.1 (1 Oct) as WTI rose on a third-carrier report.
mechanism: More Gulf crude reaching sea eases the prompt physical premium in Dated Brent.

label: Dated Brent +$20 spike
description: EIA Brent spot jumped from 114.82 to 135.51 in one day (spread 15.1 to 37.6) while futures moved about 1%, during a record week of tanker attacks (10 struck 28 Sep-4 Oct per Kpler).
mechanism: No specific trigger found. It could be a physical squeeze (record North Sea freight above $7/b), but a one-day $20 jump with no matching news may be an assessment or data artifact. Unexplained.

label: Record tanker-attack wave
description: Record tanker attacks, with only 7 tankers transiting on 6 Oct, then the heaviest attack day on 11 Oct (6+ ships; flows fall to 2.9M bbl). Spread 29.2 (6 Oct) to 31.9 (8 Oct) to 35.0 (12 Oct). North Sea grades average $127-130 in October vs Brent futures $106.
mechanism: Attacks cut Gulf seaborne exports and spike freight/war risk; the adjustment shows up in physical differentials (Dated, Forties, Ekofisk), not in WTI.

label: Nov WTI expiry squeeze
description: WTI +3% (15 Oct) on an 8.6 mb US crude draw, and the expiring Nov WTI (last trade 20 Oct) rose to +$2.39 over Dec. Brent was flat as the US weighed easing shadow-fleet sanctions. WTI spot rose 96 to 110 while Brent spot fell 126 to 115; spread 30.2 (14 Oct) to 7.3 (20 Oct).
mechanism: Prompt Cushing scarcity into contract expiry lifts spot WTI. Shadow-fleet easing would release more seaborne barrels and weigh on Dated Brent.

label: WTI roll; Houthis hit Saudi
description: After Nov WTI expired (20 Oct), spot WTI dropped back to the Dec contract (107.9 to 104.0). Houthi waves on Saudi airports/Aramco (18 Oct) and again on 22-23 Oct pushed Brent to a 6-month high ($116.72 on 23 Oct). Spread 7.3 (20 Oct) to 21.1 (22 Oct), 19.7 (27 Oct).
mechanism: Expiry roll removes the WTI squeeze premium; new Saudi supply threats lift seaborne Dated Brent. Eased a little on 27 Oct Tehran talks.
